newsitem.title: CANADA: Methanex stock boosted by new plant, pricing.
newsitem.headline: Methanex stock boosted by new plant, pricing.

text.p: Methanex Corp stock firmed in active trading Friday on positive sentiment inspired by the methanol producer's recent decision to build a new plant in Chile and strengthening prices for the chemical in Europe, analysts and the company said.
Methanex stock was up 0.20 at 11.50 in Toronto after peaking earlier at 11.80, near its year high of 11.875. Turnover was 809,540 shares, making it one of the most heavily traded issues.
Analysts said they knew of nothing new Friday to prompt the stock rise.

But they said that investor sentiment had been bolstered by Methanex's announcement Monday that it will spend US$300 million to build a third methanol plant in Chile with targetted completion in 1999. The move was seen as strengthening Methanex's efforts to lower its cost base.

In addition, a higher European contract price for methanol that went into effect a week ago was viewed as a positive sign for pricing. "Pricing now going into the fourth quarter looks to be stable if not strengthening," a company spokesman said.
The European contract price rose to 247 marks a tonne from 225.
First Marathon analyst Doug Gowland said it appears Methanex "can live and almost thrive on current pricing."

He forecast earnings of US$0.33 a share for 1996 and US$0.40 a share for 1997. He said he would be reassessing his current buy recommendation on Methanex stock since it was approaching his target of 12.

Methanex is also hoping to acquire a new low-cost methanol plant in Trinidad. The company said it had made an offer to the Trinidad government to acquire its 69 percent stake in the Trinidad Tobago Methanol Co which has yearly capacity of a million tonnes.

Methanex said it had hoped for a response from the Trinidad government months ago but does not know when the deal might move forward. The Methanex spokesman said estimates that it would be prepared to pay about US$350 per tonne of new capacity were "in the ballpark."
